text:
karen: Heads up — bought a Eurostar ticket for a client workshop using my personal card because the booking tool blocked the company card. Charge is €72.50 (converted $78.12). Ticket vendor says VAT invoice available by email but I didn't get it. cc @omar
omar: If personal card, submit expense with original vendor email + screenshot. For VAT invoices we need the vendor invoice for reclaim. Did you try the vendor portal?
karen: Portal requires ticket ref. I have the PDF e-ticket and the banking screenshot showing the charge. I requested invoice via vendor support ticket #EV-4123 and got auto-reply saying wait 48hrs. I can forward email when received. For now should I submit with supporting docs?
sam: Finance: submit now with e-ticket + bank screenshot and note "VAT invoice pending via vendor support #EV-4123". We'll process a provisional reimbursement for the net amount; VAT reclaim will be adjusted when invoice is received. Also include corpcard last4 if you used it — you said personal so include "Personal-XXXX".
karen: Submitted on Expensify: https://expensify.com/report/eurostar-216 (attached pdf e-ticket + bank screenshot). Note added. Requesting full amount reimbursement; VAT to be handled after invoice.
expensify-bot: Expense received: Report eurostar-216, total $78.12, status 'Submitted' — awaiting finance review.
omar: One more accounting detail: if vendor invoice includes VAT, finance will reclassify VAT to recoverable and adjust expense. If invoice never arrives, VAT is non-recoverable and policy caps foreign travel tickets to company-approved bookings. Since this was an exception, manager approval needed. @sam can you confirm manager sign-off?
sam: Manager exception recorded: travel booked on personal card due to company card block; approve reimbursement of $78.12 pending VAT invoice. Karen please forward vendor invoice when it lands and we'll reconcile.
karen: Thanks all, forwarding invoice when it lands.
